compsNote: 1 of the 3 competitors are within 1 km. Only executive condos are compared (an EC sells below private condos because of its buyer rules). Near-twins come first: up to two condos within 1.5 km with a similar number of homes (half to double) completed in 2016 or later. Then every suitable condo within 1 km (same tenure, completed 2011 or later first), widening to 2 km and 3 km only if fewer than 3. Resale prices are URA medians for the last 6 months where there were at least 5 resales, otherwise the last 12 months. Condos launched before June 2023 measured their areas under the old rules (including air-con ledges), so their psf is raised 5% to compare like for like.
priceDecide: Like for like by size: for each unit type we take each resale competitor's average psf for units within about 15% of that size (last 6 months, or 12 or 24 if too few). Where a competitor has too few resales of a size, that size is estimated from its own nearest size, so every unit type is judged against the same competitors. Each is raised by a new-launch premium that rises with each competitor's age (35% to 55% here): launches selling now in the OCR charge about 9% over a just-completed resale and about 2.6 points more for each year of its age (30 launches against 107 of their resale competitors, this one and the 6 most extreme pairs left out). Buy at or below = the average of the competitors' new-launch equivalents for that size (a launch nearby from the last 2 years counts for half); walk away above = 5% more. 3-bed: buy at or below $1,770, walk away above $1,860, this project about $1,792 psf; 4-bed: buy at or below $1,800, walk away above $1,890, this project about $1,800 psf; 5-bed: buy at or below $1,820, walk away above $1,910, this project about $1,806 psf. This project's price by unit type follows how psf changes with size in launches selling now (developers' caveats, 27 launches): it changes little, about +1% per sq ft for a unit twice the size. The developer breaks even at about $1,520 psf (EdgeProp's method); launches since 2023 priced on average 27% above break-even, which points to about $1,930 psf.

exit.note: At launch an EC bought from the developer is capped by the 30% mortgage servicing ratio (MSR) and a $16,000 household income ceiling; resale buyers after the minimum occupation period face only the 55% TDSR. How we test each buyer group, in today's money (prices, HDB values and incomes tend to rise together): the unit at today's expected price; a 25% down payment plus Buyer's Stamp Duty; HDB upgraders put their flat's sale proceeds in first (median resale price, minus an illustrative $150,000 loan). The group can buy if that capital covers the down payment and stamp duty; the income the remaining 30-year loan needs (tested at 4% under the 55% TDSR) is shown against SingStat's 2025 averages by home type, excluding employer CPF (4-room $11,097, 5-room and executive $13,887, condo $22,006). HDB resale prices rose 4.2% a year over the past 10 years, so upgraders' capital usually grows too. Singaporean HDB owners who buy before selling pay 20% Additional Buyer's Stamp Duty upfront and get it back only if they sell the flat within 6 months (IRAS).

supply.ring: outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD)
concerns: Will too many new condos nearby hurt my price?

Besides this project's own 430 homes, about 908 new homes within 2 km launch within about 2 years of it (Woodlands Drive 17 EC (Sim Lian), Norwood Grand); the condo resale market within 2 km handles about 82 resales a year. Our test of 33 condos completed 2016 to 2022 in the outer suburbs (11 km or more from the CBD): those with more than 1,817 other new homes completing within 2 km and 2 years grew 4.0% a year over the past 4 years, against 4.3% for those with fewer (URA caveats). Supply nearby is not a big concern here.
The developer paid more for the land. Am I paying more?

Across 16 launches since 2023, launch prices rose roughly dollar for dollar with break-even (about $103 per $100), so developers kept a similar dollar margin while their percentage margin shrank (22% above break-even on land of $1,200 psf ppr or more, 31% on cheaper land). Part of that is location: dearer land is usually where homes sell for more anyway. So a high bid does show up in prices, but only as far as buyers will pay against nearby homes. The test that protects you is the price against same-size competitors: our buy-at and walk-away prices.
Will the developer cut prices later?

Developers must sell every unit within 5 years of buying the land or repay most of a 40% stamp duty (IRAS). That pushes them to price to sell at launch; slow sellers sometimes offer deals near the deadline, but the best stacks rarely get cheaper.
Should I wait for the next launch nearby?

The next launch nearby, Woodlands Drive 17 EC (Sim Lian), is likely at about $1,960 psf, above this project's 3-bed. Waiting for it is unlikely to get you a cheaper new home here, and a dearer neighbour helps support this project's resale price.

Islandwide, about 18,296 private homes complete in 2027 and 2028 and 15,810 homes in the pipeline were still unsold at mid-2026 (URA). That is enough to keep price growth moderate, but local supply and the local buyer pool matter more for your resale.
